title: ListView and DetailView
description: Display lists of objects and single object details using generic views.

slides.title: Generic Views: The Shortcut 📋
slides.content:
Django provides **generic class‑based views** for common tasks. They handle many details automatically.

- `ListView` – displays a list of objects.
- `DetailView` – displays a single object.

You only need to specify the model (or queryset) and a template.

slides.title: Using ListView
slides.content:
from django.views.generic import ListView
from .models import Post

class PostListView(ListView):
    model = Post
    template_name = 'posts/list.html'  # optional, defaults to app/model_list.html
    context_object_name = 'posts'      # variable name in template, default is object_list
    ordering = ['-published_date']     # order results

# In template, you can iterate over {{ posts }}

quizData.question: What is the default template name for a ListView on a model named `Post` in an app `blog`?
quizData.explanation: The default is `app_name/model_name_list.html`. For app 'blog' and model 'Post', it's `blog/post_list.html`.

slides.title: Using DetailView
slides.content:
from django.views.generic import DetailView
from .models import Post

class PostDetailView(DetailView):
    model = Post
    template_name = 'posts/detail.html'  # default: blog/post_detail.html
    context_object_name = 'post'

# The view automatically captures a URL parameter like `pk` or `slug`.
# In urls.py:
path('post/<int:pk>/', PostDetailView.as_view(), name='post_detail'),

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Override `get_queryset()` for custom filtering

In ListView, you can filter results by overriding `get_queryset()`. For example, to show only published posts: `return Post.objects.filter(is_published=True)`.
